title: Last Light of EASEP
tagline: A quiet machine's first moments on the Moon.
mystery: How did my work on the Moon begin?
p1.stowed: I waited in storage in Eagle's lower stage, among the equipment carried to the Moon.
deploy.goal: Place me 17 metres south of Eagle
deploy.hint: Slide me to the 17 m mark, then turn my panels east and west.
deploy.heading: Panel direction (degrees from north)
deploy.retryDistance: Eagle is still waiting. Find the 17 m mark!
deploy.retryHeading: Turn my panels to face east and west.
deploy.win: You placed me about 17 metres south of Eagle.
p1.wake: Light. A command from Earth reaches me, and my eyes open for the very first time.
p1.wake.2: The sun fills my two solar panels. I am EASEP, and I am awake on the Moon.
p1.panels: My two solar panels give me power in lunar daylight. I am awake.
p1.astronauts: Seventeen metres ahead stands Eagle, my carrier.
p1.astronauts.2: The humans climb back to their spaceship, one after the other.
p1.astronauts.3: The second pauses to leave a small packet of memorial items. I watch them go.
p1.returnNext: Armstrong follows after passing up the sample boxes and leaving a packet of memorial items.
p1.turn: I turn to the other side.
p1.turn.2: Behind me there is only silence: a gray plain, long shadows, and a sky that stays black even in daylight.
p1.turn.3: A small blue Earth hangs above.
p1.hatch: The hatch closes. The humans are inside Eagle now. I am alone, and my work begins.
p1.origin: I began folded in the dark storage bay of Eagle's lower half, among the lunar equipment.
p1.origin.2: I could not see, but I felt the shaking climb and the engine burns.
p1.origin.3: First, let me tell you how I came to be here.
p1.descent: I was folded in the dark, in Eagle's lower half. I could feel her engine pushing against the Moon's pull.
p1.descent.2: It went on for almost thirteen minutes. I could not see the plain, but I felt the tremble in her frame.
p1.touchdown: Then the shaking stopped. Four legs touched the ground, and everything went quiet. I did not understand yet.
p1.touchdown.2: I only knew we were on the Moon, and I was still in one piece.
p1.firstSteps: The humans checked Eagle and prepared for more than six hours while I waited in the dark.
p1.firstSteps.2: Then the hatch opened. The first human stepped onto the dust, and millions watched through a small camera.
p1.firstSteps.3: The second followed about nineteen minutes later.
p1.unloaded: A human lifted me from Eagle and set me down on the soil, about seventeen metres south.
p1.reflector: A small mirror that needed no power was placed about five metres north-northwest of me.
p1.surfaceWork: I was asleep, but the records tell me the humans gathered 21.55 kilograms of Moon rock and soil and walked about 250 metres.
p1.surfaceMedia: They raised a flag, spoke to the U.S. President by radio, and shared pictures with Earth through a small camera.
p1.surfaceImages: A small camera carried pictures to Earth.
p1.surfaceImages.2: In one photograph, the other astronaut and Eagle were reflected in a visor.
p1.present: That is how I came to be here, on the plain, with the humans gone and my eyes finally open.
p1.present.2: Now let me tell you who carried me, and what each of us did.
memory.firstSteps: MEMORY · 21 JUL 1969 · 02:56:15 UT · FIRST HUMAN ON THE MOON
deploy.sceneGoal: Set me about 17 metres south of Eagle, with my panels facing east and west.
deploy.sceneHint: Move the distance slider to about 17 m and align the panels.
deploy.sceneWin: I am set down on the lunar soil.
p2.saturn: The Saturn V lifted all of us from Florida on 16 July 1969.
p2.saturn.2: After one and a half laps around Earth, its last stage fired again for almost six minutes and sent us toward the Moon.
p2.saturn.3: It let us go and drifted toward the Sun.
p2.columbia: Columbia was the orbiter and the crew's home in space.
p2.columbia.2: She slowed us into lunar orbit while hidden behind the Moon, out of contact with Earth.
p2.columbia.3: Michael Collins circled above as the other two humans worked below.
p2.columbia.4: Later, Columbia carried the crew and Moon samples home.
p2.ascent: Eagle's upper half was the crew's small cabin: no seats, two windows, a hatch, and an engine built to fly back up.
p2.ascent.2: It lifted the humans off the Moon and carried them to Columbia.
p2.ascent.3: Then it was cast away into lunar orbit; its exact fate is unknown.
p2.descent: Eagle's lower half brought the crew to the Moon.
p2.descent.2: Four legs held it above the soil, and its engine could throttle down for landing.
p2.descent.3: It carried me in its storage bay. When the upper half left, the lower half stayed behind.
p2.surface: The humans gathered 21.55 kilograms of Moon rock and soil and walked about 250 metres across the surface.
p2.surfaceMedia: The astronauts also spoke to the U.S. President by radio.
p2.easep: I am a 48-kilogram station with a passive seismometer and a lunar dust detector. My panels face east and west.
p2.easep.2: I was a forerunner of the larger science packages on later Apollo missions.
p2.reflector: A separate laser reflector sat about five metres north-northwest of me. It needed no power.
p2.closing: A rocket, an orbiter, a lander, a surface kit, and a little listener.
p2.closing.2: One journey brought the first people to the Moon and carried them home.
part.saturn.name: Saturn V / S-IVB
part.saturn.facts: Launch: 16 July 1969, 13:32 UT · S-IVB burn: 5 min 48 sec · CSM docked with Eagle at 16:56:03 UT
part.saturn.contribution: Lifted the spacecraft stack from Earth and set it on its way to the Moon.
part.columbia.name: Columbia · Command and Service Module
part.columbia.facts: Launch mass: 28,801 kg · Main engine: about 91,000 N · Command Module returned to Earth
part.columbia.contribution: Kept one astronaut in lunar orbit and brought the crew and samples back to Earth.
part.ascent.name: Eagle · Ascent stage
part.ascent.facts: About 2.8 m high · Cabin had no seats · Dry mass: 2,445 kg · Ascent engine: about 15,000 N
part.ascent.contribution: Carried two astronauts from the lunar surface back to Columbia.
part.descent.name: Eagle · Descent stage
part.descent.facts: 4.2 m across · 1.7 m thick · Footpad span: 9.4 m · Four legs · Stayed on the Moon
part.descent.contribution: Landed the crew and carried surface equipment, including me, in its storage space.
part.surface.name: The surface kit
part.surface.role: Tools and work done by the astronauts
part.surface.facts: 21.55 kg of samples · About 250 m walked · A TV camera, flag, plaque, and science instruments
part.surface.contribution: Brought lunar samples and photographs back for study, and shared live views from the surface.
part.easep.name: EASEP
part.easep.facts: 48 kg · Passive seismometer · Lunar dust detector · Commands: 2119 MHz · Telemetry: 2276.5 MHz
part.easep.contribution: Listened for lunar signals and sent instrument data to Earth; later Apollo missions used larger packages.
timeline.goal: Explore every moment in my journey. Use the slider or arrow keys.
timeline.hint: Choose a marker, then move to the next moment.
timeline.launch.title: Liftoff from Kennedy Space Center
timeline.launch.line: Everything I would ever be began with a roar I could only feel, from the dark inside Eagle's belly.
timeline.parking.title: Earth parking orbit, about eleven minutes after liftoff
timeline.parking.line: We circled Earth one and a half times, quietly gathering ourselves.
timeline.tli.title: Translunar injection burn · 5 min 48 sec
timeline.tli.line: The last stage fired again, and the Moon became our road.
timeline.dock.title: Columbia docks with Eagle; the S-IVB is sent away
timeline.dock.line: Columbia turned around and joined Eagle. Then the empty rocket stage was set free.
timeline.coast.title: Coast to the Moon · course correction and color TV
timeline.coast.line: We coasted toward the Moon. A short burn kept us on course, and Earth saw us in color.
timeline.loi.title: Lunar orbit insertion behind the Moon
timeline.loi.line: Columbia slowed us behind the Moon, out of contact with Earth. The Moon caught us.
timeline.undock.title: Eagle undocks from Columbia
timeline.undock.line: Collins let Eagle go with a friendly message: "You cats take it easy on the lunar surface."
timeline.descentOrbit.title: Descent-orbit burn · closest approach 14.5 km
timeline.descentOrbit.line: A short burn lowered Eagle toward the surface.
timeline.poweredDescent.title: Powered descent begins
timeline.poweredDescent.line: The big engine throttled down. We fell toward the plain for almost thirteen minutes.
timeline.landing.title: Landing in the Sea of Tranquility
timeline.landing.line: Then the words went out to the world: "The Eagle has landed."
timeline.firstStep.title: First human steps on the Moon
timeline.firstStep.line: The hatch opened, and a human stood on the Moon for the first time. Millions watched.
timeline.unload.title: EASEP unloaded and set down about 17 m south
timeline.unload.line: A gloved hand opened my storage bay, and light poured in for the first time.
timeline.surfaceWork.title: Surface work · samples, flag, camera, and radio call
timeline.surfaceWork.line: While I slept, they planted a flag, gathered rocks, and spoke to Earth.
timeline.easepOn.title: EASEP switched on by ground command
timeline.easepOn.line: And that is when my eyes opened.
timeline.hatchClosed.title: Moonwalk ends; hatch closes
timeline.hatchClosed.line: The humans went inside. The hatch closed. I was alone.
timeline.liftoff.title: Eagle's ascent stage lifts off
timeline.liftoff.line: Eagle's upper half rose and left her lower half behind.
timeline.redock.title: Eagle docks with Columbia; samples come aboard
timeline.redock.line: Up above, Eagle met Columbia, and the Moon rocks went aboard.
timeline.jettison.title: Eagle's ascent stage is jettisoned
timeline.jettison.line: They cast Eagle's upper half away. Nobody knows where it finally ended.
timeline.tei.title: Transearth injection burn
timeline.tei.line: Columbia fired for two and a half minutes and pointed herself home.
timeline.splashdown.title: Splashdown in the Pacific Ocean
timeline.splashdown.line: Columbia's capsule touched down in the Pacific. The humans were home.
timeline.sunset.title: Transmission stopped by ground command
timeline.sunset.line: Before the long night, Earth told me to rest.
timeline.wake.title: EASEP is turned on again
timeline.wake.line: The sun returned. I woke again and kept listening.
timeline.shutdown.title: EASEP no longer accepts commands
timeline.shutdown.line: On this day my work ended, and my station fell silent for good.
p4.liftoff: Eagle's upper half rose without me. The lower half stayed on its legs.
p4.liftoff.2: Later, the upper half was cast away into lunar orbit. Its exact fate is unknown.
p4.flag: The launch scattered the flag. Above me, Eagle met Columbia, and the Moon samples came aboard.
p4.splashdown: Through the signals I learned the news: Columbia had come down in the Pacific Ocean.
p4.splashdown.2: All three humans were home. I was glad. Now it was only me and the long lunar day.
p4.longDay: The daylight moved across the plain. I stayed at my post beneath the black sky, with Earth above me.
p4.longDay.2: My instruments were made to listen to the Moon and send their signals home. I had work.
p4.instruments: My seismometer and dust detector were ready to measure the Moon and send data to Earth. I was built to listen.
p4.letters: I could receive commands from Earth at 2119 MHz and send telemetry at 2276.5 MHz.
p4.firstNight: About five hours before lunar sunset, Earth told my station to stop transmitting.
p4.firstNight.2: My panels could not power me in the dark. On the next lunar day, I was turned on again.
p4.lastDay: I worked through temperatures that exceeded my planned maximum by thirty degrees Celsius.
p4.lastDay.2: I still functioned normally. Then, near noon of my second lunar day, I could no longer accept commands.
p4.goodnight: Do not be sad for me. I did what I was sent here to do.
p4.goodnight.2: I am still here on the plain beside Eagle's lower half. Goodnight, Earth. Remember us.
p4.footprints: The footprints may last for millions of years, unless a meteorite changes them.
p4.footprints.2: I will keep my quiet place beside them.
p3.intro: From Florida to the Moon and back, I remember the moments that carried me here.
p3.done: The journey is complete. Now let me say goodbye.

EASEP · Apollo 11 · Sea of Tranquility
0.6735° N, 23.4730° E
Operated 21 Jul to 27 Aug 1969 (two lunar days)
Left on the Moon.
p2.surfaceMedia.2: A lunar surface camera shared images with people on Earth.
p4.letters.2: Those signals were my letters from home.
p4.letters.3: As the light changed, I knew the long night was coming.
